summary:
TerraScope is an interactive Earth science data analysis platform designed to identify, visualize and investigate long-term environmental trends using NASA Earth science datasets.

The platform addresses the challenge of understanding how environmental variables change over time and how these changes differ across geographical regions. It enables users to select environmental variables, define geographical locations, specify analysis periods and examine whether observed changes represent statistically significant trends.
details:
TerraScope is an interactive Earth science trend analysis platform designed to investigate how environmental variables such as temperature, precipitation and wind change over time and across geographical regions. It allows users to select variables, time periods and locations, and visualize environmental changes through interactive maps and graphs. Using statistical methods such as Linear Regression, Mann-Kendall testing and Sen's Slope, it identifies increasing and decreasing trends, measures their magnitude and evaluates their statistical significance. It also includes Monsoon Mirror, a specialized investigation of historical Indian monsoon rainfall patterns across five geographical regions.

The main benefit of TerraScope is that it simplifies environmental data analysis by combining data exploration, statistical testing and geographical visualization in one platform. It helps identify regional differences and opposing trends that might be hidden by larger geographical averages. Its intended impact is to make Earth science data more accessible and useful for students, researchers and environmental analysts, supporting a better understanding of environmental changes through evidence-based analysis. Its creative aspect lies in combining multiple statistical techniques with interactive geographical trend discovery and regional comparisons, rather than simply displaying environmental measurements.

The project was developed using Python, Flask, NumPy, SciPy and PyMannKendall for backend development and statistical analysis, along with HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend. Plotly is used for interactive charts, Leaflet for geographical visualization, and the NASA POWER API and MERRA-2 dataset form the basis of its environmental data workflow. CARTO and OpenStreetMap provide map tiles, while Render is used for deployment. Claude was also used as an AI-assisted coding tool. During development, factors such as data reliability, missing observations, seasonal variations, statistical accuracy, autocorrelation, geographical resolution, usability and computational efficiency were considered. The application also distinguishes statistical significance from the mere presence of a trend and communicates the limitations of its analysis.
